chunks: If a man purchases a sacrificial camel while it is emaciated, it does not suffice for him. But if he purchases it as fat and then finds it emaciated, it suffices for him. And regarding the hady of the Mutamattiʿ, the same applies.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْ: it was sufficient and validly discharged the duty
key_terms.الْبَدَنَةَ: a sacrificial camel offered in ritual slaughter
key_terms.تُجْزِي: it suffices or fulfills the required obligation
key_terms.عَجْفَاءَ: emaciated, lean, and lacking sufficient flesh
key_terms.هَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering presented in hajj

ai.seo_question: Does an emaciated sacrificial animal count for hady in Hajj al-Tamattuʿ?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the validity of a sacrificial animal in hajj offerings. An animal knowingly purchased as defective and emaciated is not sufficient, while one bought as apparently sound and later found emaciated is accepted; the same rule applies to the hady of Hajj al-Tamattuʿ.
